$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later. Expected packets worked out from OpenRGB's C++ (commit d4798c120659ec5ba2e664a9e87bedff8d36f880, Controllers/CorsairPeripheralController) by a separate reference model that mirrors CorsairPeripheralController.cpp, CorsairK55RGBPROXTController.cpp and CorsairK65MiniController.cpp function by function, buffer by buffer (openrgb-work/batch2/corsair-peripheral/gen.py in the porting session's scratch space, not part of the repository); plugin.js was never run to make them. 'products' lists every product id of CorsairPeripheralControllerDetect.cpp with the variant it is tested against and its detector rule; 'extra' adds runs with the ISO layout and with the feature-report fallback of ReadFirmwareInfo. A variant gives the firmware-info reply the mock device returns (payload = the 64 bytes after report id 0x00, on the input-report path 'read' or the feature-report path 'feature'), the LED names and grid cells (HueDeck's grid; OpenRGB's LED order), two colour sets in LED order, and the I/O for Initialize (OpenRGB's controller constructor), a frame with each colour set and Shutdown (black, through the same per-frame path). ops: write = output report (hid_write), send_report / get_report = feature report set / get, read = input report read; hex is the whole buffer at the length the C++ passes, report id first. HueDeck deviation modelled here: the keyboard layout comes from the USB product id instead of bytes 0x0E-0x0F of the reply (see docs/hardware/corsair-peripheral.md). The K55 RGB PRO XT's last colour packet reads 8 bytes past OpenRGB's 411-byte colour bank; they are zeros here.
